characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis, Darjeeling-type clones

description.short: Light, aromatic Himalayan black tea from India's only state-run tea garden
description.overview: The sole tea estate in the Himalayan state of Sikkim, perched on mountain slopes near Darjeeling, sharing a remarkably similar terroir, elevation, and flavor profile.
description.leaf: Twisted, light brown leaf with fine tips
description.aroma: Floral and light, filled with cool Himalayan mountain freshness
description.taste: Mellow, fragrant, slightly gentler and smoother than classic Darjeeling
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → medium-depth oxidation → drying

history.origin: Temi Tea Estate was established in 1969 by the royal government of the Kingdom of Sikkim (then an independent state) as an initiative to employ Tibetan refugees.
history.development: Following Sikkim's integration into India in 1975, the garden remained government-operated, standing as the only tea producer in the entire state.
history.modern: Sikkim became India's first 100% certified organic state, an eco-friendly achievement shared by the agricultural practices of the Temi plantation.
interestingFacts: Temi is the only state-owned tea garden in India, distinguishing it from the privately held estates across Assam and Darjeeling.
In 2016, Sikkim was declared the world's first fully organic state, giving Temi tea pristine organic pedigree.
